_comment: Providers are data. Only two adapters exist in code — 'openai' (any endpoint
speaking the OpenAI schema) and 'anthropic'. Adding OpenAI proper, Groq,
DeepSeek, OpenRouter or Gemini's compat endpoint is an entry here, not a
Keys are read from the environment. Never write a key into this file or into

providers.label: Anthropic
providers.free_tier: none — paid from the first token
providers.notes: Own message schema, hence its own adapter.

providers.label: xKiro
providers.free_tier: reported ~5M tokens/day free (~15M with a free Telegram-verified upgrade) — third-party-sourced, not xKiro's own published docs; verify against actual usage before depending on it
providers.notes: OpenAI-compatible gateway, many providers behind one key. Model ids are vendor/model, e.g. minimax/minimax-m3:free. Auth accepts Authorization: Bearer or x-api-key, either works.

providers.label: Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint
providers.notes: Set base_url and default_model when selecting this. Covers OpenRouter, Groq, DeepSeek, Together, or a llama.cpp server on another machine.

providers.label: Google (Gemini embeddings)
providers.free_tier: 1,000 requests/day, 100 RPM, 30K TPM per model (gemini-embedding-001 and gemini-embedding-2 each get a separate 1,000/day pool) — confirmed against a real account's usage dashboard, not just docs
providers.notes: Embedding only — runtime/embed_api.py talks to it directly (batchEmbedContents, not the OpenAI chat schema), so `adapter` and `context_tokens` are unused placeholders here, same reason fish-audio's entry has them.

providers.label: Fish Audio (direct)
providers.free_tier: s2.1-pro-free is $0/M UTF-8 bytes; 5 concurrent requests per key on the Starter (<$100 paid) tier
providers.notes: TTS only — runtime/voice_api.py talks to it directly (msgpack body, not the OpenAI chat schema), so `adapter` and `context_tokens` are unused placeholders here, kept only so this entry fits the same Provider shape the LLM roles read `id`/`api_key_env`/`base_url` off of.
